label: last two copy-phase steps (short sequences or certain input letters)
explanation: Copy-phase unit (96% of activation mass) concentrated at the end of the copy: the last output step (to_go=0) holds 68% of mass and the second-to-last 23%. Rate is much higher for short sequences (L=3: 33% of steps active, L=4: 15%) and drops for L>=8. The strongest activations are on the final step of L=3 sequences (e.g. q b 3 <DEL> q [b]). Magnitude and firing are also modulated by the input token (the token just copied): b, v, n, k, p, m, f, a, u, j fire most; digits fire less. A small part (~4% of mass) is in the original phase at t=2. Almost never fires at t=0,1, at the delimiter, or at original-phase steps t>=3. Late copy steps with long L and non-preferred tokens are often silent, so precision is limited (~0.47); the token preference is not a clean category.
